title: The explicit q-hypergeometric series is the torus-equivariant small genus-zero quantum K-theory J-function of complex Grassmannians
author: Alexander Givental; Xiaohan Yan
source_title: Quantum K-Theory of Grassmannians  and Non-Abelian Localization
difficulty_reason: The proof computes the residues of the proposed series at every torus-orbit cover and matches them with the stable-map deformation Euler classes. It separately verifies the root-of-unity condition by constructing finite-difference operators over a completed lambda-algebra and specializing the auxiliary Novikov variables. These two different localization checks are needed to identify the actual stable-map J-function, rather than only a formal quasimap series.
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 018, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.018; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Full author Theorem2.6 proof, including both fixed-point tests, is supplied. X=Gr(n,N)(C),1<=n<N, with the standard diagonal T^N action and tautological K-theory roots P_i; formal equivariant weights Lambda_j, the Novikov-adic completion and the exact dilaton factor1-q are retained. The assertion is J^T(0)=(1-q)J^T for the printed hypergeometric series; it is the small stable-map quantum-K J-function, not merely a quasimap generating series. Prior fixed-point characterization and point-target finite-difference invariance [11,13] are identified background. The new explicit orbit-cover residue/Euler calculation and root-of-unity Gamma-operator specialization are fully written. The non-equivariant, cotangent-twisted, level-structure and quantum-Lefschetz variants are not separately counted.

editorial_warning: Physical page8 final operator-product display prints a sum over 0<d1,...,dn, although the preceding q-exponential expansion and Theorem2.6 both explicitly sum over nonnegative degrees, and the displayed degree-preserving operators retain the constant term. Preserve the printed strict inequality in that intermediate display; the selected theorem scope is the nonnegative-degree series actually stated in2.6.
